targetWords.definition: If something happens altogether, it happens completely. — The company stopped using sugar altogether in its food.
To bind is to bring people together.
targetWords.example: The victims of the flood were bound by their need to help each other.

targetWords.definition: A bruise is a dark mark caused by being hit by something.
targetWords.example: She got a bruise on her knee from falling down.

targetWords.definition: A custom is a way of doing things that has been the same for a long time.
targetWords.example: It is a custom that the bride and groom have the first dance.

targetWords.definition: When someone is disobedient, they do not follow the rules or instructions.
targetWords.example: The disobedient children didn't listen to their mother and had an accident.

targetWords.definition: To foresee something is to know about it before it happens.
targetWords.example: The teacher didn't foresee any problems with her large class.

targetWords.definition: glimpse [giimps] *
targetWords.example: She glimpsed outside the window as the plane was about to land.

targetWords.definition: A hoop is a ring that is made of plastic, metal, or wood.
targetWords.example: The boys tried to toss the ball through the basketball hoop.

targetWords.definition: Misfortune is bad luck or an unlucky event.
targetWords.example: His family helped him when he encountered misfortune.

targetWords.definition: When something is negative, it is unpleasant or sad.
targetWords.example: She doesn't like to say negative things about her friends.

targetWords.definition: Per is used to mean "each" when giving a price, size, or amount.
targetWords.example: It costs $8 per person to watch the baseball game.

targetWords.definition: To plead is to ask for something you want very badly.
targetWords.example: He pleaded for his parents to let him go to the soccer game.

targetWords.definition: To rip something means to pull it apart.
targetWords.example: She ripped the paper in half by accident.

targetWords.definition: The sake of something is the reason for doing it.
targetWords.example: ■ The parents worked hard for their children's sake.

targetWords.definition: To scrape something is to rub it very hard with something sharp.

story.title: Gwen's New Friends
story.passage:
Gwen walked into the gym for her next class. Coach Peeves said, "Today, we're playing

basketball. The custom is to let you choose your own teams. However, we're going to do

things differently."

The coach assigned each girl to a team. There were six girls per team. Gwen glimpsed

at her teammates. She didn't know any of them. All of her friends were on the other teams.

She couldn't believe her misfortune.

"I feel sick. May I go to the nurse?" asked Gwen.

The coach could foresee Gwen's excuses. It wasn't the first time Gwen tried to leave

class. With a stern voice, the coach said, "No."

Gwen was vehement. "I don't know any of these girls! Let me play on another team.

Please!" she pleaded.

"Gwen, don't be disobedient. I don't want to hear any more negative comments from

you."

Gwen had no choice. Then a girl smiled at her. "Hi, I'm Stephanie. I was in your English

class last year," she said. Gwen remembered her. "For the sake of the team, please try

your best. I know you're a good player," said

Stephanie.

When the game started, Gwen played

as best as she could. She took a long shot.

The ball sailed through the air and went

right through the hoop!

"That was awesome!" said one of

her teammates. Later, Gwen fell with

a loud thump.

"Are you OK?" asked her

teammates. They were worried.

She had ripped her jeans. She

had scraped her knee and had a

small bruise.

Gwen told her teammates,

"My knee is fine, and I can

stitch my pants later. Let's keep

playing!"

By the end of the game,

Gwen forgot altogether that

she hadn't wanted to play, and

her team won! The victory bound

Gwen's team together. She had made

a lot of new friends, and they were a

source of happiness for her for many

years.
